remove setuptools runtime dependency

The setuptools version is already fixed by the time `install_requires` is parsed (by setuptools).
Build dependencies can be specified with `setup_requires` if so desired.

commit message:
Added "ignore = dirty" to nupic.core submodule

`ignore = dirty` option avoids that git include the word -dirty in the end of the submodule SHA when files in a submodule folder are changed.. If these changes aren't reverted, it's impossible synchronize nupic repo with a "dirty" submodule.. 

As we should pull PRs directly from `nupic.core` repo cloned to our machine, not from its `/nta` subfolder in `nupic`, I think is simpler ignore the changes were in `/nta` and so avoid typing commands to ignore manually these changes..

I saw several developers that recommend this option:

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/3240881/git-can-i-suppress-listing-of-modified-content-dirty-submodule-entries-in-sta

http://www.nils-haldenwang.de/frameworks-and-tools/git/how-to-ignore-changes-in-git-submodules

https://github.com/bronson/vim-update-bundles/issues/32

commit message:
Spatial pooler bug fixes and improvements

Fixed bug in initialization of minActiveDutyCycles. This bug was causing boosting to occur very aggressively in the beginning. This in turn causes the SP to learn bad SDR’s.

Added separate spatial_pooler_compute_test.py for doing end to end tests of the compute function. We primarily had unit tests of the individual methods before with no tests of compute. This test is relatively basic but will catch some failures that the other tests do not.

Started implementing a test of SP boosting. Currently only Phase 1 is implemented.

Added printParameters() to the python spatial pooler to match the CPP ones. This is helpful for debugging.

The new spatial poolers will now print out the main construction parameters if spVerbosity >= 1

Improved some of the comments.

commit message:
Separate observing of Note and MergeRequests

* Move is_assigned? and is_being_xx? methods to IssueCommonality

  This is behavior merge requests have in common with issues. Moved
  methods to IssueCommonality role. Put specs directly into
  merge_request_spec because setup differs for issues and MRs
  specifically in the "closed" factory to use.

* Add MergeRequestObserver. Parallels IssueObserver in almost every way.

  Ripe for refactoring.

* Rename MailerObserver to NoteObserver

  With merge request observing moved out of MailerObserver, all that
  was left was Note logic. Renamed to NoteObserver, added tests and
  updated application config for new observer names. Refactored
  NoteObserver to use the note's author and not rely on current_user.

* Set current_user for MergeRequestObserver

  IssueObserver and MergeRequestObserver are the only observers that
  need a reference to the current_user that they cannot look up on
  the objects they are observing.

commit message:
API: tests to show incorrect behavior when reaching project limit

When reaching the project limit the API returns an error code 404 on the last possible
project. The project itself is created and is available in the database (seems valid).
A similar behavior can be observed when reaching the project limit via web client, but
in this case the user is notified that the maximum number of projects is reached. The project
itself is still created and can be accessed.

Tests are added to check the behavior when reaching the project limit or one tries
to exceed it via the API.

re-compile/re-install which is not the desired behavior and by not specifying
it on the command line, the user can always override with either a pip config
file in $HOME, or by PIP_IGNORE_INSTALLED env variable.

options too, so it makes sense to keep the pip command as light as possible.

commit message:
Fix deletion of tmp/gitlabhq-gitolite* folders in a NFS environment.

When working inside of a Vagrant box with NFS enabled, the deletion of a
repository in tmp/ doesn't work every time.

It is related to NFS inability to delete a folder if it's still used by
a resource (e.g. `rm -rf ./folder` would leave the folder and a .nfs*
    file in it). In this case it's the temporary repository which can't
be deleted because `ga_repo` is still using it.

De-allocating ga_repo is not possible (thanks Ruby), but deleting the
folder it points to in the first place fixes the issue.

Reference:
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/11228079/python-remove-directory-error-file-exists

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/19637164/c-linking-error-after-upgrading-to-mac-os-x-10-9-xcode-5-0-1

I also added `-std=c++11 -lc++abi` according to this:

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/7016730/compiling-with-clang-using-libc-undefined-references

Tests now pass on my machine.

author: Marcus Lewis <mrcslws@gmail.com>
commit message:
Stop trying to get identical boost factors between py and cpp

It's proving to be too difficult. So our options are:

1. Use shared C code to calculate boost factors and duty cycles
   for Python and C++ SpatialPoolers
2. Don't try to make them equal. Change the compatibility test to
   make sure the boost factor is right "enough", and then force them
   to be exactly equal, similar to what we already do with
   permanences.

This change takes the second approach, which I think is the better
approach.

commit message:
Improve docstring for 'save' method and others.

I encountered some confusion recently when I was trying out the 'save' functionality for models. I have adjusted the relevant documentation to provide a more detailed reflection of the current functionality and intent of the method. I have also replaced the use of varying terminology ('experiment', 'model', 'model checkpoint') with 'model' alone, for simplicity and clarity.

While I'm here, I have also made minor adjustments to the other docstrings in the file for overall consistency, in line with suggested Python style:

"The docstring is a phrase ending in a period. It prescribes the function or method's effect as a command ("Do this", "Return that"), not as a description; e.g. don't write "Returns the pathname ..."."

commit message:
Use the omniauth-ldap info object instead of the raw ldap info in extra.

This helps with compatibility with more LDAP providers as the implementation
doesn't depend on the exact names of the LDAP fields. The LDAP strategy
helps maps the attributes to the fields in the info object and we use the
info object to get the email and name.

This makes the LDAP auth compatible with most OpenLDAP servers as well.

Speed up the "Project Network Graph" cucumber feature

This change involves stubbing out the call to `Grit::Commit.find_all`
and limiting the number of commits to 10 vs. the standard of 650 used by
`Gitlab::GraphCommit.to_graph`.

Prior to this change, this single feature required almost 3 minutes of
running time and over 2 GB of memory on my machine. Now it takes less
than 3 seconds.

commit message:
Fix Wiki migration task and add more test coverage.

There was an error in the #extract_attributes_from_page method that
caused an exception when checking to see if a page named "Home"
already exists.

The check occurs to handle the renaming of the main index page to
"Home" to match the Gollum standard. If there is already a page
called "Home" then the migrator will leave that page and create
the Index page as usual. Users will need to manually rename their
old "Home" page to something else then rename their "Index" page
to "Home". Fortunately, I would be highly surprised if this case
ever comes up.

I also added more verbosity to the logging so if an error does
occur, it will be easier to track down which Wiki page is causing
the problem.

commit message:
Reserved slots to unknown categories in CategoryEncoder

Adds reserved slots to categories that are yet unknown at the time of creating the Category Encoder. When a new category is fed, the Encoder will update one of the reserved slots to encode that new category. If the Encoder runs out of reserved slots, it will return the <UNKOWN> category representation, as usual.

commit message:
removed strstream from SharedPythonOStream

This commit includes what seems like an unrelated change in svm.cpp, but it seems that
the previous SharedPythonOStream implementation was making up for a misreported persistent_size
in the svm_parameter object.

I believe the final two string recastings of close in the SharedPythonOStream class to be the
place where the string length got adjusted, but I'm not sure exactly how that worked.

Furthermore, the SharedPythonOStream object has undergone substantial changes because it
was previously internally sharing a character buffer between a strstream and a PyString object.
Using stringstream, this is not possible, so any code relating to it is removed.

commit message:
Creating or updating a MR returns more informative status codes.

Using the API library to create or update a merge request at the moment a 404 error is returned.
This is fine when the merge request in question does not exist, but does not provide good
information that for example a required attribute is missing.
A status code of 400 (Bad request) is returned when creating or updating a merge request
when either `source_branch` or `target_branch` is missing. A status code of 409 is returned
when `source_branch` and `target_branch` are the same. Tests are added for these cases.

Autolinks to issues in commit message (see #155)

It matches #[0-9]+ in commit messages.
For example
 * Fix for #12
 * Code review for #56
 * Test for #15, Review on #54, Fix for #42

 It only links to valid issues (existing and belonging to the current project)
 It does not add any link to the commit in the issue page, it only consists in parsing the commit message when displayed.

 This can be considere as a primary work for the issue #155 on gitlabhq/gitlabhq.

author: VonC <vonc@laposte.net>
commit message:
Fix git group detection for gitolite ssh user.

The tasks gitlab:env:info mixes user and group, and presume as a group 'git'.
However, gitolite group name can be anything.

That patch add the git group name in the config,
and check gitolite.ssh_user group against git.group
(which defaults to 'git', as before this patch, if undefined).

M config/gitlab.yml.example:
  Add 'group' in 'git' section
  Mention default value for the two extra settings
M lib/tasks/gitlab/check.rake:
  Check that gitolite.ssh_user *group* is the one defined in git.group.
  Make sure to default to 'git' as the expected group
    if said group is undefined in the config.
  Note: uses a more complete regexp for the group detection
        (the group can start, end or be in the middle or the list of groups
         of gitolite.ssh_user)
M: config/initializers/1_settings.rb:
  Add default values for gitolite.group and gitlab.user

commit message:
Internally public projects

Public projects listed in the public section will be linked to the
actual project's page. Public projects now give any user Guest
permissions to the project, allowing them to download the code, read
and create issues, and view anything else in the project's pages.

Ample access tests have been added to the project_access_spec to
verify correct permissions and behavior on public projects.
- Visitors to the site who are not logged in still cannot view the
  project's pages.
- Logged-in users visiting a public project where they are not a team
  member can create issues, but not snippets. They can view the projects
  code, issues, merge requests, etc, just as if they were a Guest member
  of the project.
- Since this is a public project, the user is also granted :download_code
  permissions, a permission normally reserved for Reporters, since they
  can clone the repo anyways and browse commits and branches locally.

add fallback if matplotlib is not working properly

we've been experiencing some issues with matplotlib installed with pip
(on Macs, some Linux missing freetype etc), one suggestion was to remove it completely,
as the fucntionality is only needed for some visualisations and examples.

This way we can keep it around for users who need it, we install it, if it runs on system, we're fine,
if there are problems, we fallback to option where it's not used (tests pass fine, some examples might be broke)

See https://issues.numenta.org/browse/NPC-371 and PR #141

Minor namespace fixup to be a wee bit more self-documenting of the intent.

Users of nupic should import validate from nupic.data.jsonhelpers, which may
also raise a ValidationError, also in nupic.data.jsonhelpers namespace, and
which is a subclass of ValueError.  With this changeset, it's obvious that
the ValidationError defined in nupic.data.jsonhelpers is explicitly the
implementation from Validictory.  Should we need to change it to a different
implementation, the assignment would change.

commit message:
Mac OSX compatibility changes

I had to change CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET to 10.7. Apparently that is a compatibility mode that makes the compiler use older libraries.  This is documented here:

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/19637164/c-linking-error-after-upgrading-to-mac-os-x-10-9-xcode-5-0-1

I also added `-std=c++11 -lc++abi` according to this:

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/7016730/compiling-with-clang-using-libc-undefined-references

Tests now pass on my machine.

commit message:
Removing the --ignore-installed CLI option.  When present, numpy will always
re-compile/re-install which is not the desired behavior and by not specifying
it on the command line, the user can always override with either a pip config
file in $HOME, or by PIP_IGNORE_INSTALLED env variable.

Ultimately, we'll be getting rid of --find-links, --no-index, and --index-url
options too, so it makes sense to keep the pip command as light as possible.

commit message:
Boost test complete (hopefully)

Fixed bug in how the tie breakers are used in do inhibition. In the implementation a random tie breaker is generated on every iteration. This leads to different SDRs for the same input, even if no learning or other changes have occurred. We do need a small random tie breaker, but the random offsets can be set during initialization.

Implemented phase 4 of boost test. This test is now complete.   Made test a bit more robust to randomness by increasing the number of columns. Turned learning off to isolate boosting related effects.

they're potentially expensive checks. The nupic.core math code was written to
become faster with NTA_ASSERTIONS_ON disabled, and it's best to keep it that
way.

Since the unit tests expect this param checking, implement it on the Python
side.

commit message:
Improve docstring for 'save' method and others.

I encountered some confusion recently when I was trying out the 'save' functionality for models. I have adjusted the relevant documentation to provide a more detailed reflection of the current functionality and intent of the method. I have also replaced the use of varying terminology ('experiment', 'model', 'model checkpoint') with 'model' alone, for simplicity and clarity.

While I'm here, I have also made minor adjustments to the other docstrings in the file for overall consistency, in line with suggested Python style:

"The docstring is a phrase ending in a period. It prescribes the function or method's effect as a command ("Do this", "Return that"), not as a description; e.g. don't write "Returns the pathname ..."."

author: Abe Voelker <abe@abevoelker.com>
commit message:
Fix gl-setup PATH warning when executing gl-system-install.

My git user uses bash (so .bash_profile), but I think it should work the same for sh shell.

Full warning message:

                ***** WARNING *****
gl-setup is not in your $PATH.

Since gl-setup MUST be run from the PATH (and not as src/gl-setup or such),
you must fix this before running gl-setup.  The simplest way is to add

    PATH=/home/git/bin:$PATH

to the end of your bashrc or similar file.  You can even simply run that
command manually each time you log in and want to run a gitolite command.

Run /home/git/gitolite/src/gl-system-install -h for a detailed usage message.

commit message:
API: changed status codes for project hooks functions

Different status codes in the API lib are returned on hook creation, update or deletion.
If a required parameter is not given (e.g. `url` in `/projects/:id/hooks/:hook_id`) status
code 400 (Bad request) is returned. On hook deletion a 200 status code is returned, regardless if
the hook is present or not. This makes the DELETE function an idempotent operation. Appropriate tests
are added to check these status codes.

in the svm_parameter object.

commit message:
API: refined status code handling when adding or updating a project member

When a user is added to a project that is already a member of, a status code 201 is now returned to
signal an idempotent operation. If something fails then instead of returning error code 404 different
more specific error codes are returned. Status code 400 (Bad request) is returned when a required
attribute, e.g. `access_level` is not given or 422 if there is a semantic error, e.g. should
the `access_level` have an unsupported value.

Specs are added to check these status codes.

to the "Index" page which is no longer the default Wiki page.

This commit changes the Cancel button in the following ways:

  * Pressing Cancel while editing an existing Wiki page will now

    Wiki Home page.

  - runWithConfig (accepts config dict)

  - runWithPermutationsScript (accepts path to permutations.py)

permutations_runner directly:

commit message:
A single CMake file with all build information

A new and improved CMake file.

Improvements:
- Replacement of all CMake files to a single file in order to ease understanding and maintenance (this avoids several files scattered in the repository).
- Environment variables (PATH, PYTHONPATH, NTA_ROOTDIR, etc) are set in own CMake file.
- Now it use the own Swig executable and dependencies located on External folder. Before this, I used 'find_packages' which could set an incompatible version for Nupic.
- Now it use the system python, i.e. the python package called from shell natively (similar to what Autotool version does). Before this, I used 'find_packages' which could set wrong python interpreter or libraries.

Build result: SUCCESS (including Swig modules!)

Tests results:
HtmTest: SUCCESS in all tests!!
TestEverything: 99.9107 %, only 1 (out of 2238) test failed: get spec of the dynamic library (i.e. libcpp_region).

commit message:
Handle LDAP missing credentials error with a flash message.

If a user fails to provide a username or password to the LDAP login
form then a 500 error is returned due to an exception being raised
in omniauth-ldap. This gem has been amended to use the omniauth
error propagation function (fail!) to pass this exception message to
the registered omniauth failure handler so that the Rails application
can handle it approriately.

The failure function now knows about standard exceptions and no longer
requires a specific check for the OmniAuth::Error exception added by
commit f322975.

This resolves issue #1077.

Signed-off-by: Pat Thoyts <patthoyts@users.sourceforge.net>

commit message:
Replaces datasethelpers with pkg_resources.

- Added example data location to setup.py as package data.
- Added example/prediction/data files to MANIFEST.
- Updated tests to use pkg_resources to fetch data files.
- Updated example code to fetch data through pkg_resources.
- Used pkg_resources to load files in nupic.data code.
- Removing datasethelpers and tests.
- Updated tests to write data files into examples/prediction/data.
- Updated experiment runner to resolve paths better.
    - The experiment stream source could be an absolute path or a
      path relative to the "examples.prediction.data" pkg_resource.  Updated its logic to identify absolute paths and convert relative paths through pkg_resources.
    - Updated swarming test configuration.
        - A bunch of the swarming test configurations were expecting datasethelpers to find the input file on a search path that doesn't exist anymore. I solved this by:
            - moving test_data.csv from tests/swarming/nupic/swarming/data into the package_data directory in the "swarming" folder
            - adding __init__.py to the swarming folder mentioned above
            - updating ModelRunner to call normalizeStreamSources(), which now does the pkg_resoruces lookup
            - updating all the description files to refer to "swarming/test_data.csv"

commit message:
Revert "Fix for unicode decode exception that could occur in swarming"

This reverts commit 86abd8a4b5654f247a9420bfe4a721dde2b90aa3.

This applies a patch that was previously applied in an internal Grok project,
but didn't make it into NuPIC.  In some circumstances, the error message
contains binary data that cannot be decoded properly as utf-8.  This patch
handles such failure modes gracefully.

Complete output of `git format-patch pymysql-0.5 --stdout`, comparing
pymysql-0.5-devNupic to pymysql-0.5:

From e7efaf56cbbb37af2a082a593952ef35269fe708 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Austin Marshall <amarshall@numenta.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Sep 2013 13:38:28 -0700
Subject: [PATCH 1/2] Graceful fallback in the event of UnicodeDecodeError

---
 pymysql/err.py | 12 ++++++++++--
 1 file changed, 10 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/pymysql/err.py b/pymysql/err.py
index b4322c6..56c3392 100644
--- a/pymysql/err.py
+++ b/pymysql/err.py
@@ -122,11 +122,19 @@ def _get_error_info(data):
     if is_41:
         # version 4.1
         sqlstate = data[4:9].decode("utf8")
-        errorvalue = data[9:].decode("utf8")
+        try:
+            errorvalue = data[9:].decode("utf8")
+        except UnicodeDecodeError:
+            errorvalue = repr(data[9:])
         return (errno, sqlstate, errorvalue)
     else:
         # version 4.0
-        return (errno, None, data[3:].decode("utf8"))
+        try:
+            errorvalue = data[3:].decode("utf8")
+        except UnicodeDecodeError:
+            errorvalue = repr(data[3:])
+        return (errno, None, errorvalue)
+

 def _check_mysql_exception(errinfo):
     errno, sqlstate, errorvalue = errinfo
--
1.8.2.3

From eb961a7727f6851a8962f4cc2f995e34f5ffebb1 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Austin Marshall <amarshall@numenta.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Sep 2013 13:43:13 -0700
Subject: [PATCH 2/2] Specify nupic-specific version number

---
 pymysql/__init__.py | 4 ++--
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/pymysql/__init__.py b/pymysql/__init__.py
index c1e6d03..654ed07 100644
--- a/pymysql/__init__.py
+++ b/pymysql/__init__.py
@@ -23,7 +23,7 @@ THE SOFTWARE.

 '''

-VERSION = (0, 5, None)
+VERSION = (0, 5, 'devNupic')

 from constants import FIELD_TYPE
 from converters import escape_dict, escape_sequence, escape_string
@@ -110,7 +110,7 @@ def thread_safe():
 def install_as_MySQLdb():
     """
     After this function is called, any application that imports MySQLdb or
-    _mysql will unwittingly actually use
+    _mysql will unwittingly actually use
     """
     sys.modules["MySQLdb"] = sys.modules["_mysql"] = sys.modules["pymysql"]

commit message:
Spatial pooler bug fixes and improvements

Fixed bug in initialization of minActiveDutyCycles. This bug was causing boosting to occur very aggressively in the beginning. This in turn causes the SP to learn bad SDR’s.

Added separate spatial_pooler_compute_test.py for doing end to end tests of the compute function. We primarily had unit tests of the individual methods before with no tests of compute. This test is relatively basic but will catch some failures that the other tests do not.

Started implementing a test of SP boosting. Currently only Phase 1 is implemented.

Added printParameters() to the python spatial pooler to match the CPP ones. This is helpful for debugging.

The new spatial poolers will now print out the main construction parameters if spVerbosity >= 1

Improved some of the comments.

commit message:
A single CMake file with all build information

A new and improved CMake file.

Improvements:

Replacement of all CMake files to a single file in order to ease understanding and maintenance (this avoids several files scattered in the repository).
Environment variables (PATH, PYTHONPATH, NTA_ROOTDIR, etc) are set in own CMake file.
Now it use the own Swig executable and dependencies located on External folder. Before this, I used 'find_packages' which could set an incompatible version for Nupic.
Now it use the system python, i.e. the python package called from shell natively (similar to what Autotool version does). Before this, I used 'find_packages' which could set wrong python interpreter or libraries.
Build result: SUCCESS (including Swig modules!)

Tests results:
HtmTest: SUCCESS in all tests!
TestEverything: SUCCESS in all tests!
Python tests: SUCCESS in all tests!

commit message:
A single CMake file with all build information

A new and improved CMake file.

Improvements:

Replacement of all CMake files to a single file in order to ease understanding and maintenance (this avoids several files scattered in the repository).
Environment variables (PATH, PYTHONPATH, NTA_ROOTDIR, etc) are set in own CMake file.
Now it use the own Swig executable and dependencies located on External folder. Before this, I used 'find_packages' which could set an incompatible version for Nupic.
Now it use the system python, i.e. the python package called from shell natively (similar to what Autotool version does). Before this, I used 'find_packages' which could set wrong python interpreter or libraries.
Build result: SUCCESS (including Swig modules!)

Tests results:
HtmTest: SUCCESS in all tests!
TestEverything: SUCCESS in all tests!
Python tests: SUCCESS in all tests!

  error: ‘f’ was not declared in this scope, and no declarations were found by argument-dependent lookup at the point of instantiation [-fpermissive]

commit message:
Removing the --ignore-installed CLI option.  When present, numpy will always
re-compile/re-install which is not the desired behavior and by not specifying
it on the command line, the user can always override with either a pip config
file in $HOME, or by PIP_IGNORE_INSTALLED env variable.

Ultimately, we'll be getting rid of --find-links, --no-index, and --index-url
options too, so it makes sense to keep the pip command as light as possible.

commit message:
Don't crash when removing a user that's not project member

The attempt to revoke project access for a user that was not member of the
project results in a 500 Internal Server error where it actually should
result in a 200 OK since after the operation, the user is not member of
the project. This turns the operation into an idempotent call that can
be repeated with no ill effects.

Updated the spec and changed the code accordingly. However, the result differs
slightly, as we can't return the users project access level if the user was not
member. I'm not aware if anybody relies on the result of this call.

Fixes #2832

commit message:
Updated build system to resolve [NPC-120], including addressing Marek O's comment/concern here:
https://issues.numenta.org/browse/NPC-120?focusedCommentId=10029&page=com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.issuetabpanels:comment-tabpanel#comment-10029

Also improved build system to work with a Python 2.7 install on OS X, and made it "more generic" by removing hard coded paths to 2.6 (for example, in RegionImplFactory.cpp).

The requirements.txt file no longer specifies the precise version of a dependency, but instead allows all major versions to support the Semantic Versioning model:
http://semver.org/

The reasoning being that major version bumps indicate a breaking change (not backwards compatible), while all other changes should be backwards compatible. This keeps NUPIC up-to-date with the latest improvements to its dependencies, and any issues that arise will be dealt with appropriately on an as-needed basis.

Also updated OS X build with proper linker flags for 'nta_platform_python_libs' by using the `python-config --ldflags` command. This approach should be used on the other systems as well, however because I wasn't able to test on those systems I left the those platform sections alone.

Also fixed an issue where _PY27 wasn't defined and yet was needed by several files to work properly with Python 2.7.

commit message:
Extracted CLI from Permutations Runner.

- Pulled all options parsing into run_swarm.py.
- Refactored runPermutations into lots of little pieces.
- Replaced runPermutations with three functions:
  - runWithConfig (accepts config dict)
  - runWithJsonFile (accepts path to JSON config file)
  - runWithPermutationsScript (accepts path to permutations.py)
- Updated run_swarms to call into permutations_runner.runWithJsonFile or
  .runWithPermutationsScript

So CLI is still entact, and new public functions exist for using the
permutations_runner directly:

- nupic.swarming.permutations_runner.runWithConfig
- nupic.swarming.permutations_runner.runWithJsonFile
- nupic.swarming.permutations_runner.runWithPermutationsScript

commit message:
Fix WebHook and special symbols in credentials

When using web hook with credentials secured web resource, one needs to
put the credentials in the hook URL.

If the credentials contain special symbols (e.g. @ or #), it should be
URL-quoted (e.g. %40 instead of @).

But when Gitlab is making a request, it should unquote the symbols
before base64-encoding them.

still able to access the hooks separately. For example if access to
`GET /projects/:id/hooks` fails and returns a `403 Unauthorized` error it is
still possible to access a hook directly via `GET /projects/:id/hooks/:hook_id`.

Fixes access, also added tests to check access and status codes of hooks.

commit message:
Replace current Wiki system with Gollum Wikis.

This commit replaces the old database backed Wiki system with the
excellent Gollum git based Wiki system.

The UI has been updated to allow for utilizing the extra features
that Gollum provides. Specifically:

* Edit page now allows you to choose the content format.
* Edit page allows you to provide a commit message for the change.
* History page now shows Format, Commit Message, and Commit Hash.
* A new Git Access page has been added with the Wiki Repo URL.
* The default page has been changed to Home from Index to match
the Gollum standard.

The old Wiki model has been left in tact to provide for the
development of a migration script that will move all content stored
in the old Wiki system into new Gollum Wikis.

commit message: Modified the `repo_dump` and `repo_restore` rake tasks to properly dump and restore repositories based on their `path` rather than their (project) `name`. The project name can be uppercase and may contain spaces. This caused the repository to be restored as a different `path` that it was initially created as, thus, breaking the `git remote` and the web interface can no longer detect the repository either because it searches by `path` and not by `name`. Also, when restoring the permissions are incorrect making it impossible to push new commits to the remote repository. So now on success it'll set the correct permissions (but requires that the `gitlab` user has `sudo` privileges, or this task must be executed as root).

commit message:
Create Wiki migration task.

This commit adds a new Rake task for migrating all of your existing
Wiki content from your database into new Gollum repositories.

The bulk of the logic happens within the `WikiToGollumMigrator`
class which is decently test covered and located in the lib directory.

The new Rake task can be executed by running:

   `bundle exec rake gitlab:wiki:migrate`

It will output a nice log of every project that it migrates along
with success or failure messages.

I have used it on my own installation to migrate my Wikis successfully.

Updated Hotgym to use the new class. Updated some of the Hotgym parameters to provide improved predictions.

Added checkpoint stress test to cover serialization bug fixed in https://github.com/numenta/nupic.core/issues/13

This is all part of Issue #340

author: Marcus Lewis <mrcslws@gmail.com>
commit message:
Get the C++ TM running in the integration tests

Main changes:

- Stop using so many static class variables.
- Fix filenames so that they end with "test.py" so that pytest runs them.
- Make TM test classes abstract. Use a derived class to specify the TM class
  and to inherit from unittest.TestCase.

This change backs away from using static class variables. They do bad things
when the class is used by multiple tests in a single pytest run. For example,
before this change the command

~~~
py.test extensive_temporal_memory_test.py
~~~

succeeds, but

~~~
py.test extensive_temporal_memory_test.py extensive_temporal_memory_test.py
~~~

fails.

author: Sebastian Ziebell <sebastian.ziebell@asquera.de>
commit message:
API: fixes a few return codes for project snippets

When using project snippets via API the functions now provide status codes for
different situations other then only returning 404 error. If required parameters are missing,
e.g. `title` when creating a project snippet a 400 (Bad request) error is returned. The snippet
delete function now is idempotent and returns a 200 (Ok) regardless if the snippet with the
given id is available or not. Changing return codes of these functions has the advantage that
the 404 error is used only for resources, which are not available.

Tests added to check these status codes when handling project snippets.

commit message:
Replaces datasethelpers with pkg_resources.

- Added example data location to setup.py as package data.
- Added example/prediction/data files to MANIFEST.
- Updated tests to use pkg_resources to fetch data files.
- Updated example code to fetch data through pkg_resources.
- Used pkg_resources to load files in nupic.data code.
- Removing datasethelpers and tests.
- Updated tests to write data files into examples/prediction/data.
- Updated experiment runner to resolve paths better.
    - The experiment stream source could be an absolute path or a path relative to the "examples.prediction.data" pkg_resource. Updated its logic to identify absolute paths and convert relative paths through pkg_resources.
- Updated swarming test configuration.
    - A bunch of the swarming test configurations were expecting
datasethelpers to find the input file on a search path that doesn't
exist anymore. I solved this by:
        - moving test_data.csv from tests/swarming/nupic/swarming/data into the package_data directory in the "swarming" folder
        - adding __init__.py to the swarming folder mentioned above
        - updating ModelRunner to call normalizeStreamSources(), which now does the pkg_resoruces lookup
        - updating all the description files to refer to "swarming/test_data.csv"

obj/grad/hess: refactor evaluation API

the intent of this commit is to refactor the API for objective,
gradient and hessian evaluation, such that the evaluation code
does not have to be duplicates across functions that calculate different
combinations of those functions

* introduce EvaluationTargets class that handles selection of what to evaluate
* add evaluate!(EvalTargets, ...) methods for loss and imply objs
that evaluate only what is required
* objective!(), obj_grad!() etc calls are just a wrapper of evaluate!() with proper targets

* objective!(), obj_grad!() etc calls are just a wrapper of evaluate!() with proper targets

commit message:
Improve show/hide/toggle using key presses

Previously, pressing space or enter with the channel table in focus could toggle a single selected channel - but not all of them.
Now it's possible to show/hide/toggle all selected channels by pressing S/H/T or Enter/Backspace/Space respectively. The reason for two options is that S/H/T is more 'logical' (at least in English...) but requires more keyboard searching - whereas the other keys are typically easy to find quickly, if you know the option is there.

commit message:
Revised projects

Projects have been substantially revised, and are not (yet?) backwards compatible. Changes include:
* ImageServers are serialized as JSON objects
* Numeric IDs are used rather than UUID for directory names
* When removing entries, the associated data can optionally be moved to the trash
* JsonImageServerBuilder now exists to help construct servers from JSON when stored as separate files
* Further changes to Project and ProjectImageEntry interfaces

GUI improvements:
* Improved behavior & defaults when setting pixel sizes; a hierarchy update is fired when changes are made to update measurements
* Errors are shown to the user when projects cannot be opened

commit message:
Use cached tiles with ImageDisplay histograms

Use whatever low-resolution cached tiles we can find when calculating histograms within `ImageDisplay`.
This is used for auto-setting or resetting the brightness/contrast.

The rationale is:
* We want to construct an `ImageDisplay` quickly, so we don't want to have to visit all the z-slices and time points for a large image just to build a histogram.
* We want to make the best estimate we can of the min/max and overall histogram within the Brightness/Contrast dialog, without requiring that we read an infeasibly large number of pixels.

For this to work, we assume that we're using an `AbstractTileableImageServer`. There's a good chance this performs less well with ImageJ z-stacks, so that behavior will need to be checked.

commit message:
Don't build histogram from large image stacks

QuPath builds a histogram when opening an image, and this is used for Brightness/Contrast settings. This is usually based on a low resolution image and works fine. But it *doesn't* work fine for large z-stacks or time series, especially if these are at a single resolution.

It also isn't fine when opening remote images, e.g. stored through OMERO.

This PR uses a *very* basic approach to select only the middle slice of a z-stack in the event that reading the entire thing would require more than 50 MB to open. This makes it fast to open some images that otherwise throw out-of-memory errors.

For discussion...

author: pete <pete.bankhead@gmail.com>
commit message:
Major refactoring for Java 11

Major code refactoring with several goals:
* Compatibility with Java 11, including modularization
* Consolidation of processing code (i.e. no more ImageJ/OpenCV decision; permit both to be used together, with other key libraries)
* Increase the chances of finding a suitable packaging solution to create cross-platform installers

There remain many limits... e.g. modularization is incomplete. because it was incompatible with some dependencies (e.g. OpenCV with JavaCPP); the biggest challenge is the need for multiple modules not to use the same package names.

This also resulted in some QuPath classes being moved, and in general most packages are exposed in all modules... but this is probably not desirable.  So the next phase needs to look at improving the organization further.

commit message:
Improve drag & drop responsiveness

Improve responsiveness, somewhat counterintuitively, by introducing a delay.

The point is to avoid always processing drop events (e.g. to open images) directly in the `handle(DragEvent event)` method because these could take too long - especially when launching other dialogs (e.g. to set the image type, or import to a project).

This previously had the outcome that other applications (e.g. Finder on macOS) could hang for several seconds, or other temporary weirdness might occur.

By storing the files/URL that were dropped and then processing them after a short delay (here, 50 ms) this problem can be avoided.

commit message:
PathObject changes

Switched again from TreeSet to use LinkedHashSet for child object list.

The 'trouble' with TreeSet was its use of the compareTo method to resolve whether or not to add an object; if this returned zero, only one object would be included. This may be a good thing, unless the comparator is not sufficiently reliable.  Some comparator changes have been made, but because it was only intended to give a rough ordering for reproducibility when listing objects, it is not considered reliable enough for this purpose.

Tests have been updated to assess if child list contents are the same, rather than true equality for a list or collection (which behave in different ways).  The order should be considered undefined.

Improved ConverterJTS.

author: pete <pete.bankhead@gmail.com>
commit message:
Improved tile caching

Switched to use a Guava cache, optionally setting the percentage of available memory used for tile caching in the preferences.

The hope is that this (and use of soft values) will reduce out-of-memory errors by better enforcing the cache size, while giving the opportunity to use larger caches where RAM permits. This is especially important for multiplexed images.

This means that care needs to be taken when returning null from readBufferedImage(); ideally null would not be returned since it is not a supported value in the cache.

Introduced 'empty' tiles within AbstractTileableImageServer to mitigate this. This allows sparse/pyramid-generating servers to return the same tile for multiple requests if there is nothing present (i.e. an unscanned region). This is not stored in the main cache, but rather locally within the server. The memory requirements are considered negligible.

This can dramatically reduce the number of pixel arrays being stored for sparse images, and thereby improve the usefulness of the cache.

Fixed a bug caused by delayed loading of Wand tool, where an exception was thrown if the Preferences were opened before the Wand was available.

author: Melvin <melvin.gelbard@gmail.com>
commit message:
Added '{}' block handling to Script Editor

- Added the handling of new lines following a '{' character, which works as follows:
1. A block is generally  '{' + new line + indentation + new line + '}'
2. The caret position is set to inside the block
3. If there originally was some text after '{', the text will be included inside the block. E.g. forEach{doSomething()} becomes: forEach { <new line> <indentation>doSomething()<new line>}.
4. If the amount of '{' and '}' in the text is equal, it will add the new line but won't create a block. This is to avoid cases where there already is a closing bracket. E.g. hitting 'Enter' after the opening bracket in the following example will not add a closing bracket, since one is already present: forEach { <new line> <indentation>doSomething()<new line>}.
5. A space is added before '{' if there wasn't one already (purely aesthetic)

- At this stage, this is quite experimental. However, it could develop into something more advanced in the future.

commit message:
Update build.gradle for Java 16

This involves several changes:
- Use toolchain rather than target version.
  - This is required because Gradle can't currently be run using Java 16, and so the build script needs to be called using a different Java version than the one used to build QuPath.
- Strip the version number from the application name.
  - This is required to avoid package failures due to the .cfg file name being different.
- Explicitly specify the java.library.path to be $APPDIR
  - This is required to load OpenSlide/JPen. The library path was previously set automatically by jpackage in Java 14 (but not 15).
- Explicitly use java-options in the cfg file when changing the memory settings
- Avoid setting the version on macOS
  - Sadly, we cannot start a version number with 0

These changes should also address the issues that arose when building QuPath v0.2 with Java 14: https://github.com/qupath/qupath/issues/615

Several other changes were made:
- Update gradlew
- JavaCPP now uses platform plugin for better dependency management
- Guava version updated
- License report plugin updated

commit message:
Introduce PathObjectHierarchy timestamp

Introduce `PathObjectHierarchy.getLastEventTimestamp()`... well, admittedly this was committed in error recently, and this code makes it usable.

The rationale is that sometimes we need to know if the hierarchy is changed, but it is too expensive to add/remove listeners to handle all events.

For example, an expensive lazy measurement that is calculated on demand and cached internally only needs to know whether to recompute the value *at the time when it is requested*. So it can check the object hierarchy timestamp to know whether to do the expensive calculation again, or just to return the last computed value.

Note that, as a side effect of these changes, all detection count measurements are updated automatically when interactively moving an annotation around an image. Previously, these only updated whenever the object was 'committed' to the hierarchy.

Add min/max local normalization

This applies dilation and erosion to the image to get local minimum and maximum values, then subtracts the minimum and divides by the range.

The minimum and maximum images can also optionally be Gaussian smoothed to avoid sharp discontinuities.

Like other local normalization strategies, this approach can boost the noise in an image if there is no meaningful signal.

author: pete <pete.bankhead@gmail.com>
commit message:
PathClass, wand & brush tool improvements

A new ‘Region’ PathClass is introduced that behaves slightly
differently from other classes, e.g. classified ‘Region’ annotations
are not painted as filled in even when other annotations are.
Consequently it is good for heavily annotated regions, or possibly
detected tissue containing further annotations inside.

The PathClassFactory will endeavor to improve the reproducibility of
the colors generated for a new PathClass by seeding its random number
generator according to the hashcode of the specified name.

The wand tool now optionally incorporates overlay information whenever
it calculates new shapes (this can be turned off in preferences).

The wand also takes the existing shape being edited into account,
thanks to a morphological closing being applied to the union of the
edited shape & the potential new shape being generated by the wand.
This helps avoid isolated pixels being included and creating
excessively-complex shapes.

The brush now uses less aggressive shape simplification, and ‘avoiding
overlapping objects’ (by pressing the shift key) ignores ‘Region’
objects - since it is anticipated that one probably does want to
annotate inside these.

Finally, also fixed ProbabilityColorModel bug that prevented use of
float images.

commit message:
Update multithreading support in BioFormatsImageServer

Aims to fix https://github.com/qupath/qupath/issues/865
This takes a different approach to parallelization, managing a pool of ImageReaders with each tile-requesting thread taking the next available reader.
If there are no readers available, and the total number is less than some maximum value (based upon the number if available processors), a new reader is generated on another thread and added to the queue when ready.

This should
* avoid generating more readers than needed, with a limit separate from the number of tile requesting threads
* avoid attempting to initialize multiple readers simultaneously, which can be a bottleneck

In addition, more tests have been added.

author: Pete <pete.bankhead@gmail.com>
commit message:
Simplify PathPlugin and PluginRunner

Quite a major refactoring & simplification of how `PathPlugin` implementations are handled.

The original problem was that `PluginRunnerFX` proved to be buggy with detached windows, because the `ImageData` being handled was accessed via `PluginRunner.getImageData()`. In most cases that's fine, but `PluginRunnerFX` was always returning the *current* `ImageData` from QuPath, and if this *changed* before the plugin was complete (and had fired any hierarchy updates /  logged any workflow steps) then exceptions or unexpected behavior could occur.

It might conceivably have happened previously when using multiple viewers, but I don't know of any cases where it did - because QuPath locks the UI when plugins run, and this seemed to be working ok.

The new design greatly simplifies `PluginRunner` to simple run tasks in parallel with progress notification - with some special logic for `PathTask` implementations.

Alongside that,
```java
PathPlugin.runPlugin(PluginRunner pluginRunner, String arg)
```
has been updated to
```java
PathPlugin.runPlugin(PluginRunner pluginRunner, ImageData<T> imageData, String arg)`
```
so that there's no need to request the `ImageData` from the plugin runner - and it's possible to ensure this remains unchanged, no matter what might go on in the UI.

Early indications are that the code is just simpler and more robust. However, it's still a core change that *could* potentially have broken lots of things, so most analysis-related commands ought to be checked (e.g. cell detection, or anything else involving `PathPlugin`). In particular, the ImageJ macro runner might be affected.

make getNameWithoutExtension return value consistent

`GeneralTools.getNameWithoutExtension(String)` returns the whole string
without the extension for absolute path, while
`GeneralTools.getNameWithoutExtension(File)` returns only the file name
part without the extension. eg: `/home/demo/myfile.tif`, the former
method returns `/home/demo/myfile` while the latter one returns
`myfile`. This commit make them return `myfile` for consistent. A test
is also added.

commit message:
Improve ImageDisplay initialization

Throw an `IOException` if `ImageDisplay.setImageData()` fails, and remove the constructor that takes an `ImageData` parameter in favor of adding a static `create()` method instead.

The purpose is to 'fail faster and better' if pixels cannot be read from an image, to avoid putting the viewer into an invalid state.

Previously, failure to open an image (e.g. because JPEGXR decompression was unavailable on Apply Silicon) would lead to an extremely uninformative NPE, and then possibly a lot more exceptions when attempting to interact with the viewer in any way.

When making these changes, the constructors for `QuPathViewer` were changed to no longer take an `ImageData` as a parameter. This was always null anyway (viewers were always created without an image), so makes no real difference to the current code - but the change avoids the possibility of the constructor having to throw an exception if the image couldn't be set. Now the image must be set as a second step, after the viewer has been created.

commit message:
ImageData & fluorescence data performance improvements

Changes to improve how brightness/contrast settings are managed.

These are now stored (as a JSON property) in serialized ImageData
objects.  Additionally, when repainting a serialization of these
properties is also used to construct a key for RGB tile caching.  This
is applied for image types that are expensive to paint (i.e. > 1
channel, non-RGB) because of the color transforms involved.

A small extra change: .qpdata files in a project are no longer saved
automatically if there have been no changes & no .qpdata file already
exists.  This makes the presence or absence of a .qpdata file more
informative.

Adjusting the brightness/contrast now counts as a ‘change’, and a
prompt will be added asking whether to save or not.

Finally, the auto brightness/contrast setting has been made less
extreme.

commit message:
OpenSlide and Bio-Formats fixes

Fixes mostly inspired by .scn files:
- OpenSlide now uses the image bounds, if available; without it, occasionally a small scanned region appeared as a much larger region with a huge black border (which also thwarted image type estimation)
- OpenSlide uses a default tile size of 256 if none is stored (rather than -1, then promptly throwing an exception when needing to return something)
- Bio-Formats now loads the largest series in a file, if no series is specified, rather than the first one; this helps when the first series might end up being a macro image instead of a pyramid

The downsample estimation has also been updated to give a stronger preference for using the closest power of two.

commit message:
Add icons to single measurement table

The purpose is to:
* Make classifications stand out more (with color)
* Make it possible to distinguish measurements from the measurement list, from those calculated dynamically
* Provide a visual queue to distinguish between annotations, detections & TMA cores

The last of these is done by using the same icons used for show/hide in the toolbar. The hope is that this helps reinforce the association between object type and icon.

Note that the implementation is a bit messy because we don't currently have a way to query the type of a measurement from `ObservableMeasurementTableData`. If/when this is refactored to reduce any JavaFX dependency, we should try to improve this; currently, it's not entirely robust, because someone *could* add measurements or metadata values with duplicate names.

Fixes https://github.com/qupath/qupath/issues/1220 - to an extent.

This uses a very simple approach by calculating changes to the z and t position in the main viewer, and then adding these changes to the z and t values for the viewers to be synchronized - and then clipping to the actual range of z and t values supported by the image in viewer being synchronized.

That should work nicely when synchronizing across stacks with identical dimensions, using the same z and t indices. But where dimensions or indices don't match, then out-of-range clipping can cause the relative difference between the main and synchronizing viewer to squeeze down to zero.

I'm not at all convinced that's the ideal behavior, but it should be better than ignoring z and t entirely (as is currently the case).

commit message:
Add support for custom styles

This adds support to add custom styles by adding .css files to the a css subdirectory inside the user directory (which is where extensions go, usually at ~/QuPath/v0.4/ or similar).

If the custom css directory exists, a WatchService is created to check for changes. This means that users can add/remove/modify .css files in the directory, and see live updates (albeit with some seconds of delay, at least on macOS).

To make this work, the PreferencePane needed to be updated to directly use any ObservableList with combo boxes.
A new `PathPrefs.getCssStylesPath()` was also added.

Additionally, IconFactory.DuplicableGlyph was improved to allow glyphs to respond to the `-fx-text-fill` property, and this in turn means that the toolbar icons can now be styled by css (rather than being fixed to a neutral gray).

Finally, main.css was introduced to enable more QuPath-specific styling, even when using the default modena.css with JavaFX. This is particularly relevant for defining several colors reused by the script editor.

Downsample estimation shared among ImageServers

OpenSlideImageServer now uses the same downsample estimation method as BioFormatsImageServer.  OpenSlideImageServer has also been slightly cleaned up & finally logs the version number.

commit message:
Better exception handling deserializing qpdata

Addresses
* https://github.com/qupath/qupath/issues/1252

To test this, we need a project that contains a broken (truncated) .qpdata file, and a corresponding complete .qpdata.bkp file.

If we have the last of these, we can create a truncated file in a Groovy script, e.g. with

```groovy
def full = "/path/to/data.qpdata.bkp"
def partial = "/path/to/data.qpdata"
new File(partial).bytes = new File(full).bytes[0..10000]
```

Attempting to serialize this should throw an exception. Previously, this wasn't an `IOException`, and so QuPath didn't automatically switch to the backup.... now it should.

commit message:
Fixed PathClass.compareTo method

`PathClass.compareTo` is now equivalent to
```
this.toString().compareTo(o.toString())
```

Note that in previous versions (< 0.1.2), the comparison was made based on the name only.

This could result in unexpected behavior whenever comparing with equality and using derived `PathClass` objects, because only the (final) name part was being compared and this could potentially result in classifications (wrongly) being considered equal (e.g. "Tumor: Positive" and "Stroma: Positive").

This was most significant when working with Groovy, where `==` is replaced by `compareTo`.

commit message:
Handle Bio-Formats pyramid level changes

See https://forum.image.sc/t/can-creating-detections-from-pixel-classifier-be-made-to-run-faster/96745/25
Bio-Formats 7.2.0 handles pyramid levels differently for SVS images, which would break compatibility with the metadata stored in QuPath projects. Basically, the levels stored in the project would override the levels that Bio-Formats expects to find.

Consequence: if a project was created in v0.5.1 (or earlier), including SVS images read using Bio-Formats, these images could not be opened in v0.6.0.

This PR logs a warning when this occurs, and uses the 'new' pyramid levels are used instead of the ones stored in the saved metadata.

commit message:
Add setClassification(Object) method

Add `PathObject.setClassification(Object)` as some protection from Groovy's laxness.

Otherwise, one letter makes a *big* difference. Consider
```groovy
getSelectedObject().classification = ["First", "Second"]
getSelectedObject().classifications = ["First", "Second"]
```
The second is probably intended (setting a derived class), but the first would result in a class being set to the string `["First", "Second"]` because Groovy will 'helpfully' cast the list to a string.

Adding `PathObject.setClassification(Object)` intercepts any attempts to set a classification with a non-string, so that a more informative exception can be thrown instead.

commit message:
Simplify DnnModel implementation

Remove generic parameter and move prediction & blob functions to `AbstractDnnModel`.
The motivations are:
- make it easier to implement `DnnModel`
- make it easier to handle memory management with the DeepJavaLibrary implementation

The second is because memory management seems to work best when using a `Translator` and not working directly with `NDList` inputs and outputs for prediction. This means that it's better to predict 'all at once' rather than across multiple methods (create blob, predict, convert output).

Support script args for command line

Add support for passing arguments to a command line script using the --args keyword. Multiple args can be passed by using the keyword multiple times, or by using a "[comma,separated,list]".

--server can be used to pass arguments when constructing the ImageServer with the --image option.

Fixed bug that meant the wrong tile could be provided by an AbstractTileableImageServer, because the path element of the request was ignored.

Also changed the event fired when an annotation is modified with the MoveTool, allowing it to count as an 'added' event (since the object is being re-added to the hierarchy). commit message:
Introduced TileRequest as separate class

Separated TileRequest into a separate class, and updated ImageServer interface to return all available tiles.  These are immutable, so can be retained.  This reduces the number of RegionRequests that need to be created, and makes it possible to reduce ambiguity when a consumer tries to request tiles exactly but fails due to rounding errors.  (This was occasionally resulting in issues where an intended single tile request actually required getting two tiles to add a single row or column of pixels).

Added results string to Pixel classifier pane & improved performance of object classification based on the pixel layer.  Corresponding pixels are now based on flooring double coordinates (rather than rounding), which fits with the visual appearance whenever viewing the overlay at high magnification with nearest neighbor interpolation.

Added option to control output type (classification or probability).

Improved readability of classifier names based on OpenCV StatModels & help text for RTrees parameters.

commit message:
Add more map-like syntax to MeasurementList

This mostly provides shorter alternatives to `putMeasurement(String, double)` and `getMeasurementValue(String)` (i.e. `put(String)` and `get(String)` respectively).

The intention is that it is easier to switch between using a MeasurementList or a map since the key methods have the same syntax - although only a small subset of Map methods are implemented.

The reasons to use the list are
- required for backwards-compatible serialization support
- works with primitive values

The reasons to use the map are:
- familiar API
- support for null to be returned for missing values (rather than NaN)
- more convenient with scripting
- no need to call .close() for efficiency (this is carried out internally)

commit message:
'Deselection mode' when pressing Alt

This PR addresses https://github.com/qupath/qupath/issues/1704 by changing 'selection mode' to become 'deselection mode' when the 'Alt' key is pressed.

This is comparable to how drawing tools become 'subtraction' tools when the 'Alt' key is pressed.

Therefore there are 3 different behaviors possible when drawing a ROI with selection mode turned on:
- No keys pressed - reset any current selection, and select any objects within the ROI
- Shift key pressed - add any objects within the ROI to the current selection
- Alt key pressed - remove any objects within the ROI from the current selection

Do image checks earlier in BioFormatsImageServer

Check image validity while initializing a BioFormatsImageServer to reduce the chances of adding invalid images to the available image list, which will then later fail. Also, default to largest image in a series only if it is substantially larger than the first image - otherwise stick with the first one.

Now this image should be identified as invalid and not displayed to the user.

Fix tile padding, improve tile export robustness

Fix regression that caused partial tiles to be resized to the requested tile dimensions, and bugs in how tile patches were requested.

A script to show the DnnTools patch extraction in action is below; it operates on a selected ROI and should give an image of the requested size at the requested resolution (with zero-padding, if required)

```
def server = getCurrentServer()
def roi = PathObjectTools.getROI(getSelectedObject(), true)
double d = 2.0
int w = 200
int h = 100
def mat = DnnTools.readPatch(server, roi, d, w, h)
OpenCVTools.matToImagePlus("Mat", mat).show()
```

commit message:
Updated ImageServers to use URIs

ImageServerBuilders now use URIs rather than String paths, which makes the scheme clear and helps test whether support is available more effectively.  Bio-Formats servers have been revised to take the series number as a fragment, reducing the reliance on a name being present. For backwards compatibility, a name can still be provided as a query.

The cache is no longer provided as a parameter to the constructor, but rather is taken automatically from the ImageServerProvider by any server that requires it (currently all AbstractTileableImageServers).

ImageServerProvider can now optionally take an array of preferred builders, to give control over preference.

commit message:
Improve ContourTracing efficiency

Partially addresses https://github.com/qupath/qupath/issues/1780 by replacing `Point2` with `IntPoint2`, which stores its values in a packed `long`.

This doesn't make much difference to performance for the ~5 million vertices tracing, but it *did* make it possible to trace much larger regions - making `Polygonizer` the bottleneck.

For example, I could trace two regions - with 39,230,067 and 21,436,882 respectively, in 532 seconds.

Rendering was then slow again, and I couldn't *save* them because of memory issues... but I think it indicates that this PR improves the efficiency of some parts of the tracing.

author: Pete <pete.bankhead@gmail.com>
commit message:
Improve ImageOps/pixel classification performance

Reduce memory use & computation in two main ways:
- Strip padding in `SplitMergeOp` *before* calculation, rather than after
  - This helps when the split/merge uses different amounts of padding
- Strip padding before merging channels, rather than after

Together, these can result in fewer pixels being processed, and less need to generate multiple large arrays to merge channels.

In one extreme example (fairly high-resolution pixel classifier using all RGB features across multiple scales) I saw a >20% reduction in computation time.

author: pete <pete.bankhead@gmail.com>
commit message:
Project improvements

Various improves to handling projects, including:
* Dragging a project directory containing multiple .qpproj files onto
QuPath now shows a dialog asking to choose which project to open
* Dragging an empty directory onto QuPath now results in an offer to
convert it into a project directory (i.e. a much easier way to create
projects)
* When a new project is created, generation of the ‘scripts’ directory
is delayed until it is needed - to avoid modifying an empty directory
unnecessarily
* When writing a Project file, the last version is backed up by
appending .backup to the name (an extra safety net)
* ProjectIO.writeProject(project, name) now has more sensible behavior…
making it easier to write new project files to the same directory, but
with a different name (previously QuPath would preferentially overwrite
the current file, potentially ignoring the specified name)
* Project.getName() now includes both the directory name & .qpproj file
name - to handle cases where the same directories contain multiple
.qpproj files

commit message:
Improve tiling performance when running plugins

The main aim is to avoid naively and sequentially computing the intersection of every rectangular tile with an outer geometry.
This uses several tricks:
* Use a parallel stream when computing intersections using multiple tiles
* For large ROIs, compute intersections first for all tiles in either each row or column, so subsequent intersection calculations are simplified
* For large ROIs, create a prepared geometry first to check covers/intersects quickly
Results should be the same as using the previous sequential approach with RoiTools.computeTiledROIs; the old method remains to enable testing.

Duplicate requests occur e.g. when writing an OME-TIFF using multithreading or running a pixel classifier and with a tile size larger than the tile size of the reader. It can result in the same image tiles being read multiple times, potentially adding considerable unnecessary overhead (since tile decompression can be a bottleneck).

commit message:
Improved stain setting & relaxed cytokeratin H-DAB rule

Creating cytokeratin annotations no longer performs (excessively-strict) check that the image is identified as H-DAB.  This means it can be more easily repurposed for other ROI-generating purposes.

The actual processing is unchanged so long as the third stain is a residual stain vector; Stain 2 is consideredto be the main marker (i.e. DAB previously), while the tissue is the sum of either Stain 1, Stain 2 and Stain 3 (if it is not a residual stain vector), or Stain 1 and Stain 2 (if Stain 3 is a residual stain vector).

The parameter keys are also retained, i.e. thresholdDAB is still the key even if the stain itself isn't actually DAB.

When setting stain vectors, the option to change the name is now only enabled for 'Brightfield (Other)' to prevent confusion; also, the option to specify the collective names for the stain vectors has been added.

commit message:
Improve ContourTracing performance

This makes `ContourTracing` much faster in some circumstances - especially when labeled images were involved.

There are two main differences:
1. Previously, the code would tend to loop through all pixels to generate the contour for each label; now it generates bounding boxes in a single loop, and then iterates only through the relevant bounding box for each label (when using `createROIs`)
2. The tracing algorithm has been replaced by a reliance on JTS's `Polygonizer` class; this was already used before, but now we rely on it more heavily.

The second of these makes this *slightly* risky - I encountered exceptions and infinite loops along the way, so this needs to be tested very carefully.

commit message:
Show settings changes in BC dialog

In the Brightness/Contrast dialog, update the settings combo box whenever settings are modified (e.g. sliders moved) to include an asterisk and name in italics.

This is intended to address https://forum.image.sc/t/please-help-us-test-the-qupath-v0-5-0-release-candidate/87976/23

The change is relatively conservative, aiming to avoid any substantial overhead whenever changes are made quickly. Specifically, we don't check whether and changes have been *reversed* so that the settings are now 'unmodified again'. We also don't try to handle settings being flagged as changed when switching across multiple viewers.

Therefore the asterisk and italics doesn't mean the settings are different, only that they might be different.

This could be addressed, but the tests would be more expensive to perform and therefore a little risky immediately before release, in case the performance impact is noticeable.

commit message:
Pixel classifier improvements

Pixel classifiers now require an ImageData, not merely an ImageServer.  This enables them to (potentially) use other information, such as color deconvolution stains or the image type.

RGB tile caching is applied less often in the PixelClassificationOverlay; for classified results it is not necessary for performance, and only consumes memory.  Additionally, the painting code has been rearranged so that the RGB cache tile might (in the future) outlive the original tile, which need not remain cached if memory is at a premium.  Relatedly, a memory estimate is logged when the classifier server is created.

Fixed (kind of) a bug whenever ellipse annotations were used to mask the PixelClassificationOverlay; now uses ellipse bounding box.

Delayed initialization of StatModels until they are required; this means that the Pixel Classifier window opens _much_ faster.

Removed unnecessary RGB/BGR switches in OpenCVPixelClassifierDNN, and now set it to set a channel to zero if scale is zero (it would probably be wise to change scale to a multiplication rather than a division).

commit message:
Fix Insecure Deserialization Vulnerability in UndoRedoManager

Summary
This PR fixes a critical security vulnerability related to insecure deserialization in the UndoRedoManager class. The current implementation attempts to use a ValidatingObjectInputStream but contains syntax errors and implementation issues that would prevent proper security controls from working.

Description
Java deserialization vulnerabilities (CWE-502) are among the most critical security issues in Java applications as they can lead to remote code execution. The current code in UndoRedoManager appears to have started implementing a fix for this vulnerability by using ValidatingObjectInputStream, but the implementation is broken and contains syntax errors that would prevent it from compiling.

This PR properly implements the fix by:

Correcting the variable names and syntax errors
Properly implementing the ValidatingObjectInputStream with a strict whitelist of allowed classes
Ensuring consistent error handling
Changes
Fixed the implementation of deserialize() method to correctly use ValidatingObjectInputStream
Corrected variable naming inconsistencies (bais vs stream, in vs ois)
Fixed syntax issues with mismatched braces
Ensured proper class whitelisting to prevent arbitrary class deserialization
Security Impact
This change significantly improves the security posture of QuPath by preventing deserialization attacks, which could allow attackers to execute arbitrary code on users' systems through carefully crafted serialized objects.

Related Issues and CVEs
This fix addresses vulnerabilities similar to:

CVE-2020-9484 (Apache Tomcat - Deserialization of Untrusted Data)
CVE-2020-36518 (Jackson-databind - Deserialization vulnerability)

References:
https://github.com/apache/hadoop/commit/5e2f4339fadc88f20543915fc9b0aaeaf4f9e7bf
https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2020-9484https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2020-36518

author: pete <pete.bankhead@gmail.com>
commit message:
Major ImageServer changes

Significant changes to ImageServers, with a view to making it possible to serialize and deserialize more complicated servers, e.g. to apply dynamic transforms.

* Standard ImageServers are now built using a URI and optional String arguments. This removes the need to squeeze all relevant information into a single URI or String path. The essential information for their construction can be serialized to/from JSON using the ImageServers class.
* Custom ImageServers may be derived from others, e.g. subclasses of TransformingImageServer or SparseImageServer. The most important examples of these are also supported by the ImageServers class.
* Sub-images are opened directly, rather than returning a path (since a path along is no longer adequate to construct an ImageServer).

URI's play a more key role now because these may need to be queried when a project is opened in order to ascertain whether or not a project has moved (i.e. if either absolute or relative URI's still point to valid files). However projects haven't yet been updated to handle all the changes.

On the other hand, paths are no longer what they once were. They should still be unique for caching, but can't be used to construct new servers.

commit message:
Replace makeRGB(A) with pack(A)RGB methods

The reasoning is that the previous names were confusing... makeRGBA took arguments in that order, but actually generated a packed ARGB value. It also avoided any input checks, which could potentially cause input values outside the range 0-255 to cause unexpected results.

The pack(A)RGB and packClipped(A)RGB methods take arguments as ARGB and produce a packed ARGB result, using defined methods of handling input outside the range 0-255.

The old methods remain, but have been deprecated and all uses have been updated.

commit message:
Add JavaFX to module path

See https://github.com/openjdk/jfx/blob/jfx16/doc-files/release-notes-16.md#important-changes

This change puts JavaFX where it wants to be, but can potentially cause problems - so more testing is needed. Specifically, there can be trouble where reflection is accessing internal JavaFX classes.

When issues are found, these can generally be worked around with --add-opens and --add-exports - but we need to be on the lookout for any that either QuPath or its dependencies rely upon. And ideally we wouldn't require access to anything that isn't exported.

In the longer term, QuPath itself should become modular - but this remains difficult to achieve because of its non-modular dependencies.

author: pete <pete.bankhead@gmail.com>
commit message:
ImageServer update, revision of AbstractTileableImageServer

Added getChannelName(int) int method to ImageServer.

Substantially revised AbstractTileableImageServer so that tiles are now requested using coordinates defined at the pyramid level, not in the full resolution image space.  The idea is that this should be more predictable and reproducible, avoiding differences that can potentially occur when different ImageServers use different approaches to rounding floating point values.

This then made it possible to add a prototype SparseImageServer, which requests tiles from other ImageServers corresponding to different regions to dynamically create a larger field of view.  Empty tiles are returned as null; the viewer should render these in some informative way (currently, they are shown as black).

Replace missing ImageOp categories, support JSON subtype aliases

ImageOps should have categories associated with them, so that their labels are of the form "op.filters.gaussian", for example. In v0.2, some of these categories were erroneously omitted.

These didn't cause name clashes at the time, but probably would as more ops are added... for example, "op.channels.mean" and "op.filters.mean" would be expected to do different things, but without categories could both be shortened to "op.mean".

This commit aims to reinstate categories while still being able to read legacy ops. This involved replacing RuntimeTypeAdapterFactory entirely using a different implementation that supports aliases for deserialization.

commit message:
Better building, javadocs

Support specifying toolchain with Gradle (first) or system property (second) - rather than using a gradle properly only.

This is needed because `includeBuild` requires the extension to respect the toolchain, and it is easier to as a system property that is used everywhere, i.e. within `gradle.properties` add a line such as
```
systemProp.toolchain=23
```
and then this should propagate to any included builds that use the QuPath Gradle plugin v0.2.1 (or later, presumably).

Also allow `include-extra` to have any file extension or none (shortest name is preferred). This is to make it easier to handle in an IDE, e.g. using `include-extra.properties` means that shortcuts to comment/uncomment lines can be used - but we don't want to enforce the use of `.properties` as the extension since it isn't really a properties file (it doesn't contain key-value pairs).

commit message:
Revised MiniViewerCommand, thumbnail generation and histograms

Rewrote MiniViewerCommand so that it no longer creates subclasses of QuPathViewer, but rather uses a custom Canvas component.  This should be much more efficient, and avoid the need to handle all the pain that can come from setImageData in QuPathViewer (which impacts the ImageDisplay etc.).

Among the other benefits, launching the channel viewer is much faster.  Painting is also now performed in a background thread to further improve performance.

Other changes:
- Revised histograms to make them immutable (previously could set normalized status)
- Added getDefaultThumbnail methods to ImageServer
- Revised ChannelDisplayInfo to remove setters from core interface
- Rewrote histogram-caching mechanism used with ImageDisplay
- Removed requirement for ImageRegionStore within ImageDisplay
- Removed SecondViewerOverlay (which wasn't useful)
- Added option to access last repaint timestamp in QuPathViewer

Fix problems with invalid geometries

Improved conversion of ROIs to JTS Geometry objects. Specifically, the previous approach could fail badly for objects with holes or whenever objects had self-intersections (or very nearly). This in turn led to unexpected hierarchy behavior, e.g. where objects where considered 'below' a parent even if they were actually located inside holes.

Added new tests to check for agreement between QuPath ROI measurements and Geometry measurements.

Also improved polyline centroid calculation (previously this was simply the center of the bounding box).
